title: Motion, brakes and stopping
question: If speed doubles, does the total stopping distance simply double?
task: First trace the fluid-pressure and friction path. Then compare two speeds while keeping reaction delay and effective grip unchanged.
check: I can separate reaction travel from braking distance.
answer: At unchanged reaction delay, reaction travel grows in proportion to speed. In the constant-deceleration teaching model, braking distance grows with speed squared. The hydraulic lesson explains force transfer, not a real vehicle’s stopping performance.

title: A circuit and one more appliance
question: What changes when another parallel load is switched on?
task: Trace the complete loop and parallel branches. In the virtual experiment, change one appliance and compare total current.
check: I can explain why branch currents add.
answer: Parallel branches receive the same supply voltage in the ideal model. Their currents add at the supply. Real protection and safe use depend on wiring, devices and exact ratings; keep this exploration virtual.

title: Heating, cooling and a power outage
question: Does stored warmth disappear as soon as the power stops?
task: Trace how a heat pump transfers energy. Then interrupt electric heating in What If and compare insulation or thermal mass one at a time.
check: I can distinguish heat transfer, stored energy and electrical input.
answer: The air-conditioner lesson shows a powered refrigeration loop. The outage experiment instead models an electrically heated room losing stored heat. Together they distinguish energy input from energy already in a system; neither predicts a particular home.

title: Hearing and spreading sound
question: What changes at the listener when the source moves farther away?
task: Trace the ear’s sound-to-signal pathway. Then compare listener distances from the same source in the silent What If model.
check: I can distinguish the hearing pathway from a sound-level calculation.
answer: The ear lesson describes a biological pathway. The free-field experiment shows geometric spreading and logarithmic levels under stated assumptions. It does not model rooms, individual hearing, or establish safe listening exposure.

title: Clouds, rain and water on the ground
question: Where does the same amount of rain go on different surfaces?
task: Follow condensation and precipitation. Then hold the storm constant while comparing ground infiltration and drainage.
check: I can distinguish rainfall formation from runoff after it reaches the ground.
answer: Cloud formation concerns water in the atmosphere; runoff concerns water after it reaches a surface. Soil, storage and drainage change where water goes. These simplified models are not local weather or flood forecasts.

title: Engine power and cooling
question: Can an engine produce useful motion and still need to reject heat?
task: Follow the four-stroke cycle. Then change one cooling condition in What If and compare the temperature trend from the same starting conditions.
check: I can explain why useful work does not remove the need for cooling.
answer: Combustion converts fuel energy into work and heat. The cycle cutaway and separate cooling model show different parts of that energy story. Their timing and temperatures are teaching approximations, not diagnostic instructions.
